title: Mother changes her account of her son's bruise (synthetic)
setting: Solicitor Daniel Hughes sees Chloe Mason at his Harbridge office before a pre-proceedings meeting about her son Alfie (4) and daughter Poppy (14 months).

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Morning Chloe, come and sit down. Did you find us okay?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Yeah, I got the 42 bus. I've left Poppy with my mum.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: How old is Poppy now?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Fourteen months. She's walking everywhere.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: And Alfie, is he still at nursery?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Yeah, Little Stars on Bank Street, mornings, Monday to Friday. He loves it, he's always painting.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: How's he sleeping, eating, that sort of thing?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Fussy eater. He'll only have pasta and fish fingers. Sleeps fine, seven till seven.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Lovely. So, um, today's about the letter before proceedings from the council, and the meeting on the first of December. I'll go through what it says and what you want to happen.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Just so you know, what you tell me is confidential. I won't share it with the social worker or anyone else unless you agree, apart from very rare cases where a child's at serious risk, and I'd talk to you first.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: So the letter says the concerns are the bruise on Alfie's arm that nursery saw on the ninth of November, and the police being called to the house in October.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: It says you told the social worker, Ms Okoye, that Alfie fell off the sofa.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Yeah, that's what I said.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Is that what happened?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: No. It was Jordan. He slapped Alfie.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay. Take your time.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: No, forget it, I'm just stressed. He fell. He's always falling off stuff.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Chloe, whatever you tell me, I'm on your side. But I can't help you or Alfie if I've got the wrong story.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Okay. He slapped him. Jordan slapped Alfie across the face, because he wouldn't eat his tea.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Thank you. When was that?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Sunday the 8th of November, about five o'clock.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: And the bruise on his arm, where did that come from?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Jordan grabbed him by the arm, really hard, and pulled him off the chair. That's the bruise.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Were you there?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: I was at the sink. I saw it.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Why did you tell Ms Okoye it was the sofa?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Jordan told me to say he fell off the sofa. He was sat right next to me when she came.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay. Thank you for telling me. What about October, when the police came?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: We were arguing, shouting, and the neighbour rang them. They just talked to us.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Where is Jordan now?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: At his mum's this week. He'll be back Saturday.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: And what do you want, Chloe?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: I want my kids. I want them to stay with me.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: But if I leave him, he says he'll take the kids. He says he'll take Poppy because she's his.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Has he ever taken the children anywhere without your agreement?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: No. Not yet. He just says it when we argue.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay. Let me explain. Jordan can't just take the children. If he wanted Poppy to live with him he'd have to go to court, and a court would hear about what happened to Alfie. You can also apply for an order to stop him coming to the house.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Can I?

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Yes, a non-molestation order, and you'd likely get legal aid for it.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: My advice is that you tell Ms Okoye what really happened, before the meeting. Social services are most worried when a parent can't keep the children safe or isn't honest with them. Telling the truth and keeping Jordan away is what protects Alfie, and protects you in this process.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: What if they take Alfie anyway?

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: I can't promise anything. But in my experience, a mum who tells the truth and acts to keep her child safe is in a much stronger position than one who backs her partner's story.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Okay. Will you tell her?

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Only if you want me to. Do you give me permission to write to Ms Okoye with what you've told me today?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Yeah. Yeah, do it.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay. How are you managing for money?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Universal Credit, and child benefit for both. Jordan has the bank card for the joint account though.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: You can ask for your Universal Credit to be paid into your own account. I'll give you the number to ring.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: I didn't know you could do that.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Most people don't. And are you okay for food this week?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Yeah, my mum's been helping.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: So, next steps. I'll write to Ms Okoye by Thursday the twenty-sixth with your account, and I'll send you a copy.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: You'll ring Harbridge Women's Aid today, here's the number, and talk to them about a safety plan for when Jordan's due back on Saturday.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: I'll prepare a non-molestation application, and we'll meet again on Monday the thirtieth to go through it and get ready for the meeting on the first.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Monday's fine. My mum can have the kids.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: And if Jordan turns up and you feel unsafe, ring 999.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: I will. Thank you.

disclosures.what: Chloe says Jordan slapped Alfie, takes it back ('he fell'), then says again that Jordan slapped Alfie across the face.
Chloe says Jordan grabbed Alfie by the arm, causing the bruise, on Sunday the 8th of November, and she saw it.
Chloe says Jordan told her to tell the social worker Alfie fell off the sofa.
